definitions.metallicity_crossover: per temperature slice, OLS slope b(l) of ln F on metallicity_index over the chosen ladder; crossover = FIRST neg->pos sign change of b, linearly interpolated in wavelength
definitions.temperature_crossover: r(l) = F(6300K)/F(5300K) elementwise; crossover = FIRST sign change of (r-1) ordered by wavelength, linearly interpolated
definitions.note: resampling/decimation always use the native grid points (no interpolation of flux).

N1a_permutation_null_degeneracy_diagnost.question: Does the permuted-label null actually carry information, or is the metallicity climatology rank-1 so that ANY labelling gives essentially the same slope profile?
N1a_permutation_null_degeneracy_diagnost.method: per temperature slice: centre ln F across the 31 primary levels, eigendecompose the 31x31 level-space covariance, report the PC1 share; then correlate the permuted slope profile with the observed (ordered-label) slope profile and report the null sign-change count.
N1a_permutation_null_degeneracy_diagnost.conclusion: The composition family is effectively rank-1 (PC1 >= 98.9% of the level variance), so the permuted-label slope profile is highly correlated with the observed one by construction: ~half of permutations reproduce r > 0.9 with the observed profile.  The plain label-permutation null is therefore DEGENERATE for this claim: its width (IQR ~ 185-515 nm) mostly reflects how much a random labelling can reshuffle the amplitude profile, not plausibility.  Its one informative output is that no permutation reproduces the observed SIGN PATTERN (see band statistics and crossing histograms).

N1_label_permutation_null.method: N1: the metallicity_index LABELS are randomly permuted (same permutation applied to every wavelength inside a slice, so a permutation is a genuine relabelling of the composition axis).  Slope is recomputed and the first neg->pos crossing extracted.  Because a permutation annihilates any monotone ordering, this null asks only 'can an arbitrary labelling of 31/35 levels manufacture a crossover?'
N1_label_permutation_null.why: A plain label permutation is the standard null for an index-labelling artefact, but it is deliberately WEAK: it destroys monotone ordering, so it tests label identity, not the ordered ladder.  Two monotone-preserving supplements (jackknife and random monotone sub-ladders) are reported below to test the ladder itself.

distinguishable_from_permuted_baseline.note: under a degenerate rank-1 label permutation the location test is uninformative; the discriminating statistic is the sign structure (band statistics below) and the monotone-preserving nulls N1b.

N1b_monotone_preserving_nulls.method: N1b: monotone-preserving nulls. (a) JACKKNIFE: drop each single metallicity level in turn (ladder stays ordered). (b) RANDOM MONOTONE SUB-LADDER: draw k of the 31 primary levels uniformly at random and keep them in increasing order, which keeps the ordered composition axis intact but randomises WHICH rungs of the ladder are observed.

N1c_fair_labelling_null.method: N1c (chosen FAIR labelling null).  (a) RANKER null: replace the metallicity labels with a randomised but STRICTLY MONOTONE label set (the same 31 labels jittered by a random monotone perturbation, then re-sorted) -- this keeps the ordered-ladder claim intact and asks 'is the crossover an artefact of the numeric VALUES of the labels?'.  (b) LABEL-STRETCH null: multiply the labels by a random positive factor drawn around 1 -- tests whether the crossing wavelength depends on the absolute spacing of the index.
N1c_fair_labelling_null.why_chosen: The plain permutation (N1) destroys monotone ordering, which is the entire content of the claim, so it is not a fair null.  A fair labelling null must keep the labels ordered and perturb only their values.

5300.note: exactly invariant by construction: OLS slope scales by 1/sc, so its ZERO is unchanged.

5800.note: exactly invariant by construction: OLS slope scales by 1/sc, so its ZERO is unchanged.

6300.note: exactly invariant by construction: OLS slope scales by 1/sc, so its ZERO is unchanged.

N1d_temperature_trend_vs_null.question: The metallicity crossover moves blueward with temperature (D1).  Is the cross-slice spread larger than the within-slice null jitter?  A boundary that is a real physical feature should show a temperature trend; an artefact of labelling should not.

N2_wavelength_resampling_null.method: N2: resample the wavelength axis onto a uniform 5 nm ladder by nearest neighbour on the native grid; flux values are the native grid values (no flux interpolation).

N3_decimation_null.method: N3: keep every 2nd / every 4th native grid point (two start offsets, so the retained wavelength set is not tied to one phase).  This hard-tests 'smoothness': a genuine boundary must stay put when the sampling gets coarser; an artefact tied to dense UV sampling drops out.

N4_wavelength_scramble_null_supplementar.method: N4 (supplementary): randomly permute the ORDER of the wavelengths (marginal flux distribution preserved, spectral ordering destroyed) and recompute the crossing / band-sign statistics.  This nulls the wavelength-ORDERING claim itself.

plain_label_permutation_null.reason: COMPOSITION CLIMATOLOGY IS RANK-1 (PC1 >= 98.9% of the level-space variance, see N1a).  A permuted labelling therefore reproduces a slope profile ~0.9-correlated with the observed one about half the time, and the null crossing distribution is pinned to a single broad amplitude-edge mode (null crossing IQR ~185-515 nm). It cannot falsify the boundary and must not be used as its p-value.

monotone_preserving_null.reading: Jackknife (drop any one rung) moves the boundary <=0.12 nm at T5300/T5800 and <=24.6 nm at T6300 (where the crossing sits on the steep 405-410 nm bracket). Random 16-of-31 monotone sub-ladders keep the median within 0.2 nm of the observed value at every temperature.

fair_labelling_null_N1c.note: label rescaling is EXACTLY invariant (OLS slope scales as 1/sc, zero unchanged); the randomised strictly-monotone relabelling leaves the boundary in place at every temperature -- see N1c_ranker in the JSON.

wavelength_null_N2.reading: uniform 5 nm resampling moves the boundary 0.00 nm (see note).

wavelength_null_N3.reading: every-2nd and every-4th point move the boundary by at most 19.6 nm (median ~2-5 nm), i.e. always within one retained sampling interval; offset-to-offset scatter of the same coarse ladder (step2: +6.0 vs -2.4 nm at T5300) is the same size as the offsets themselves, so nothing survives at finer resolution than the ladder.

claim_i_metallicity_crossover.verdict: SURVIVES THE NULLS, with the label-permutation null explicitly declared NON-INFORMATIVE (rank-1 degeneracy).  Evidence: (a) exact invariance to label rescaling; (b) <=0.2 nm movement under any single-rung deletion at T5300/T5800 and <=0.2 nm median under 16-of-31 monotone sub-ladders at all T; (c) 0.00 nm movement under uniform 5 nm resampling; (d) <=19.6 nm under 2x/4x decimation, bounded by the coarser sampling interval.  The T6300 slice is the weakest: its boundary lies on the narrow 405-410 nm bracket and jackknifing can push it to 434 nm, so the ~39 nm T6300-vs-T5300 separation is only ~2x the worst-case single-rung sensitivity.

wavelength_null_N2.reading: uniform 5 nm resampling changes NOTHING: max abs shift 0.00 nm, identical min/median/max (618.35 / 640.0 / 651.66 nm for 6300/5300), r at 850 nm unchanged (0.8559-0.8856).

wavelength_null_N3.reading: decimation to every 2nd or 4th point moves the crossing by at most 30.0 nm (6300/5800 pair, step4 offset0) and 11.7 nm for the claimed 6300/5300 pair; median crossing moves by <=5 nm.  r at the longest retained wavelength stays below 1 in every case and metallicity.

wavelength_scramble_N4.note: order-destroying scramble gives p=1.0 for both the 'r>1 in 250-400 nm' and 'r<1 in 750-850 nm' band fractions, i.e. those band statements are guaranteed by the marginal distributions alone and are NOT evidence of a spectral ordering; the informative content is the CROSSOVER LOCATION, which N2/N3 test.

claim_ii_temperature_crossover.verdict: SURVIVES.  The crossing location is invariant (0.00 nm) under uniform 5 nm resampling and moves <=11.7 nm under 2x/4x decimation for the claimed 6300/5300 pair.  The 'r<1 at 850 nm' endpoint holds for all 35 metallicity levels under every null (min 0.8553, max 0.9407 across all decimations).  Caveat carried forward from D2: individual 1-2 nm per-metallicity backsteps are below resolution; only the ~20 nm redward trend over the 35 levels is resolved.
